bugs: acquire() timeout validation has no isinstance check: a non-numeric timeout (e.g. '1') raises TypeError from math.isnan instead of ValueError (same in KeyedRateLimiter.acquire).
Deadline check adds 1e-9 s slack (now + wait > deadline + _TOL); with timeout=0 and a very high rate a sub-1e-9 s sleep can be issued, deviating from 'timeout=0 never sleeps' (extreme edge).
Token validation is copy-pasted in both classes.
C-0f84.summary: Correct, thread-safe implementation with LRU OrderedDict and sleep outside the lock; only minor validation sloppiness and so-so tests.

bugs: Thread-safety tests use the real clock with hard-coded elapsed-time bounds (e.g. granted <= 10 + 100*0.1 + 1), which can be flaky on a slow CI machine.
C-6b27.summary: Clean, exact-to-spec implementation with shared validators, exact deadline comparison, correct LRU and lock scoping; tests are good but the real-clock concurrency tests are timing-dependent.

bugs: KeyedRateLimiter._validate_tokens deliberately skips the tokens <= capacity check, so try_acquire(key, capacity+1) creates/bumps the key (and may evict another key) before the bucket raises ValueError - violates 'validation happens before anything else'.

acquire sleeps min(wait, remaining) instead of the computed wait, and has an extra 'remaining <= 0' bail-out path; within the +_TOL slack this can cause a spurious short sleep followed by failure, deviating from the single-sleep contract.
Tests poke private state (_level, _last_time, clk._t) and the eviction-during-block test is not actually concurrent because FakeSleep returns instantly.
C-bfd5.summary: Mostly correct bucket, but the keyed limiter violates the validate-before-side-effects rule for over-capacity tokens and the acquire loop is needlessly convoluted.

bugs: Test test_concurrent_try_acquire_no_overadmission constructs TokenBucket(0, 100), which raises ValueError, so the test errors out.
Test test_clock_goes_backwards sets clock to 50 then advances to 55 (< last_time 100) and asserts available()==5; per spec (and the implementation) it is 0, so the test fails.
max_keys=True and rate=True are accepted (bool is int); minor.
Deadline check adds 1e-9 s slack (minor spec deviation).
C-a286.summary: Solid, correct implementation with good lock discipline, but the submitted test-suite contains two tests that cannot pass.

bugs: test_solution.py contains no KeyedRateLimiter tests at all and no concurrency tests.
test_repeated_sleeps_when_early_wake contains dead code and a stream-of-consciousness comment (unused clk, calls, s2, clk2).
Deadline check adds 1e-9 s slack (minor spec deviation).
C-4321.summary: Correct and thread-safe solution with thorough validation, undermined by a half-finished test file that ignores half of the spec.

bugs: _validate_tokens/_validate_timeout use float(x), so string inputs like tokens='1' or timeout='0.5' are silently accepted.
rate/capacity validation calls math.isfinite directly: a non-numeric rate raises TypeError rather than ValueError; bool is accepted.
Validators are duplicated verbatim in TokenBucket and KeyedRateLimiter.
Deadline check adds 1e-9 s slack (minor spec deviation).
C-e3af.summary: Behaviourally correct and well documented, with reasonable tests, but input validation is loose and the code duplicates its validators.

bugs: TokenBucket.acquire(tokens) with the default timeout=None computes self._clock() + None and raises TypeError - the default blocking call (and KeyedRateLimiter.acquire with timeout=None) is completely broken.
timeout=float('inf') is rejected (math.isfinite check) although the spec only forbids negative/nan; the candidate's own test_timeout_inf_is_valid therefore fails.

Own tests test_immediate_success, test_sleep_never_zero, test_timeout_none_blocks_indefinitely, test_blocking_acquire_per_key etc. call acquire without timeout and crash; test_failed_acquire_counts_as_use calls try_acquire('A', 11) which raises uncaught ValueError.
max_keys=True accepted (bool is int).
C-949f.summary: The blocking acquire path crashes on its default argument, so the submission does not meet the spec and would fail its own test suite.

bugs: timeout=float('inf') raises ValueError although the spec only forbids negative/nan timeouts.
max_keys=True is accepted (no bool exclusion), yet the candidate's own test_invalid_max_keys expects ValueError for True, so that test fails.
test_keyed_limiter_contains_non_hashable asserts [1,2] not in lr, but __contains__ hashes the key and raises TypeError, so the test errors.
Validation uses math.isfinite without isinstance, so string rate/tokens/timeout raise TypeError instead of ValueError; validators duplicated across classes.
C-b67a.summary: Core bucket and LRU logic are correct and lock scoping is right, but validation diverges from the spec in small ways and two of its own tests fail.

bugs: test_failed_try_acquire_still_counts_as_use is an abandoned stub (body is rambling comments and 'pass').
test_other_thread_steals_wake_retry monkeypatches the private b._sleep attribute.
rate=True / capacity=True accepted (bool is int); minor.
C-1cdc.summary: Exact, well-structured implementation with shared validators, exact deadline arithmetic, correct LRU bumping and sleep outside all locks; tests are broad (early wake, steal, eviction during block) apart from one leftover stub.
